title: Cost in life energy
principle: Money is a stand-in for the hours of life you traded to earn it. Before buying something, translate its price into the hours of work it actually cost you — that reframing makes the true cost of a purchase visible in a way the price tag alone doesn't.
formula: Cost in work hours = price ÷ hourly net income.
fitsWhen: You want a gut check on whether a purchase is worth what it actually costs you in time and effort, not just money.
critique: It treats all work hours as equally unpleasant and interchangeable, which isn't true for everyone — some work is itself rewarding, so the trade isn't purely a sacrifice.
